name: Human Behavioral Biology
note: Robert Sapolsky's Stanford course on how genes, evolution, the brain and hormones shape behavior, from ethology and aggression to stress and mental illness.

name: Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute Talks
note: Symposium talks from Stanford's neuroscience institute, including 2017-2018 sessions on neural networks, reinforcement learning and brain-inspired AI.

name: Expert Tips for Behavior Change
note: Five short Stanford explainers on research-backed behavior change: habits with BJ Fogg, goal pursuit, momentum, healthier eating and big life decisions.

name: Yale PSYC 110: Introduction to Psychology
note: Paul Bloom's introductory psychology course at Yale: the brain, Freud and Skinner, how babies think, language, emotion, love, persuasion and dreams.

name: The Psychology, Biology and Politics of Food
note: Kelly Brownell's Yale course on why we eat as we do: appetite biology, food psychology and addiction, obesity, food marketing and food policy.

name: Philosophy and the Science of Human Nature
note: Tamar Gendler's Yale course pairing Plato, Aristotle, Kant and Mill with cognitive science on happiness, morality, justice and political legitimacy.

name: Experts in Emotion Series
note: Expert talks on the science of emotion introduced by June Gruber, with Lisa Feldman Barrett, Paul Ekman, Jaak Panksepp, Laurie Santos and others.

name: The Science of Well-Being
note: Twelve short lessons from Laurie Santos's Yale course on the psychology of happiness: myths about happiness, savoring, gratitude, work, money and love.

name: Moralities of Everyday Life
note: Paul Bloom's Coursera course from Yale on the psychology of morality: caring for others, strangers, empathy and its limits, plus two office hours.

name: MIT 9.00SC Introduction to Psychology
note: MIT's introductory psychology course: 24 lectures on perception, memory, development, personality, psychopathology and social behavior, taught by John Gabrieli.

name: MIT 9.00 Introduction to Psychology
note: Jeremy Wolfe's 2004 MIT introductory psychology course: brain, motivation, learning, perception, memory, thinking and development, with demonstrations.

name: MIT 9.13 The Human Brain
note: Nancy Kanwisher's MIT course on how the brain supports perception and cognition: methods, face and place areas, navigation, number, nature versus nurture.

name: MIT 9.14 Brain Structure and Its Origins
note: Gerald Schneider's MIT course on vertebrate functional neuroanatomy, tracing brain structure through evolution and development from the spinal cord up.

name: MIT 9.20 Animal Behavior
note: Gerald Schneider's MIT course on animal behavior and ethology: Konrad Lorenz, fixed action patterns, innate behavior, motivation and the evolution of behavior.

name: MIT 9.04 Sensory Systems
note: Peter Schiller's MIT course on the visual and auditory systems: retina, visual cortex, color, depth and form perception, illusions and eye movements.

name: MIT 9.40 Introduction to Neural Computation
note: Michale Fee's MIT course on quantitative models of neurons: ionic currents, Hodgkin-Huxley, dendrites, synapses, spike trains and receptive fields.

name: MIT RES.9-003 Brains, Minds and Machines Summer Course
note: Nine-unit summer course directed by Tomaso Poggio and Gabriel Kreiman: lectures on vision, memory, computational cognitive science and AI.

name: MIT 6.868J The Society of Mind
note: Marvin Minsky's MIT course on how minds are built from simpler processes: emotions, cognitive architectures, layered representations and common sense.

name: MIT 6.868J The Society of Mind
note: Five lectures from Marvin Minsky's 2007 MIT course on how minds arise from simpler processes, touching on learning, memory, emotion and consciousness.

name: MIT 9.35 Perception
note: Josh McDermott's MIT course on how the senses work, emphasizing hearing and vision: psychophysics, auditory scene analysis, retina and visual cortex.

name: MIT 14.13 Psychology and Economics
note: Frank Schilbach's MIT course on behavioral economics: time and risk preferences, reference dependence, social preferences and applications.

name: MIT 24.08J Philosophical Issues in Brain Science
note: Five lectures from Pawan Sinha and Alex Byrne's MIT seminar on philosophy and neuroscience: infant cognition, Molyneux's query, imagery, consciousness.

name: MIT 9.11 The Human Brain
note: Nancy Kanwisher's Human Brain course in 73 short segments from MIT's CBMM, starting with Marr's levels of analysis and face recognition.

name: Brains, Minds and Machines Seminar Series
note: Research seminars from MIT's Center for Brains, Minds and Machines on vision, language, theory of mind, consciousness and computational models of the brain.

name: Brains, Minds and Machines Summer Course
note: Lectures and tutorials from the 2016 Brains, Minds and Machines summer course: neuroscience, consciousness, attention, computer vision and language.

name: Psychology M176: Families and Couples
note: UCLA lecture course on communication and conflict in families and couples, taught by Benjamin Karney: relationships, marital discord and family disruption.

name: Behavioral Neuroscience Lab: Psychology 116
note: Nine lectures from UCLA's behavioral neuroscience laboratory course (Psychology 116), exploring how the brain controls behavior.

name: Intimate Relationships
note: Thomas Bradbury and Benjamin Karney's undergraduate lectures at UCLA on intimate relationships, following chapters of their textbook of the same name.

name: This Emotional Life: Common Relationship Issues
note: Eight short videos in which UCLA psychologists Thomas Bradbury and Benjamin Karney answer relationship questions from the This Emotional Life community.

name: Industrial-Organizational Psychology
note: Short promo clips and faculty spotlights for Harvard Extension courses in industrial-organizational psychology, organizational behavior and statistics. [dropped: promos, not lectures]

name: Outsmarting Human Minds
note: Three short Harvard videos from Mahzarin Banaji's Outsmarting Human Minds project on the mind's blind spots, first impressions and better decisions.

name: How America's Sleep Deficit Is Damaging Long-Term Health
note: Nine short highlights from a Harvard School of Public Health forum on sleep loss and health: poverty, school start times, shift work and tired doctors.

name: Experimental Psychology
note: Short Oxford videos on experimental psychology: depression and faces, dyslexia with Dorothy Bishop, learning to read, prejudice, ageing, brain stimulation.

name: Neuroscience at Oxford
note: A mixed collection of Oxford neuroscience videos: dementia and Parkinson's research, brain imaging, memory, stem-cell models and news features.

name: Brain and Mental Health at Oxford
note: Ten short Oxford researcher profiles on brain and mental health: sleep and body clocks, technology, psychosis, chronic pain, child and perinatal care.

name: A Romp through the Philosophy of Mind
note: Marianne Talbot's five-lecture Oxford introduction to the philosophy of mind, from the mind-body problem to consciousness and artificial intelligence.

name: Understanding Mental Health (#OxfordMentalHealth)
note: Six Oxford researchers in conversation with well-known interviewers: conspiracy beliefs, mindfulness, PTSD, sleep and dreams, and child anxiety.

name: Our Mental Wellness
note: Three Oxford talks on self-help for mental wellness: managing depression and low mood, overcoming sleep problems, and managing stress and anxiety.

name: Oxford Psychiatry
note: A mixed collection of Oxford psychiatry videos: talks on paranoia, psychological therapies, chronic pain, genes and brains, plus department news.

name: Personality and Its Transformations
note: Jordan Peterson's University of Toronto personality course (PSY230), recorded 2014 to 2017: Freud, Jung, Rogers, Piaget, Frankl and mythology.

name: Maps of Meaning: The Architecture of Belief
note: Jordan Peterson's University of Toronto seminar (PSY434) on how myth, narrative and neuropsychology shape belief systems, recorded in two-part lectures.

name: The Psychological Significance of the Biblical Stories: Genesis
note: Jordan Peterson's 2017 public lecture series on the psychology of Genesis: God and hierarchy, Adam and Eve, Cain and Abel, the Flood and Abraham.

name: PSYA01 Introductory Psychology
note: Steve Joordens's introductory psychology course at U of T Scarborough, Fall 2020: 76 short videos on the science of psychology, its history and the brain.

name: PSYC85 History of Psychology
note: Steve Joordens's U of T Scarborough course on the history of psychology, from the ancient Greeks and Descartes through Darwin, Fechner and Helmholtz.

name: NEW302 Jungian Psychodynamics
note: Anderson Todd's Toronto course on Jungian psychodynamics: the unconscious, archetypes, complexes, ego, shadow, persona, anima and animus, and the self.

name: NEW303 Hypotheses of the Unconscious
note: Anderson Todd's University of Toronto course on the unconscious: archetypes, the multiple self, mutual modelling, and endogenous and exogenous altered states.

name: BPM332 Buddhism and Psychotherapies
note: Anderson Todd's Toronto course alternating Buddhist traditions with Western psychotherapies, in the Buddhism, Psychology and Mental Health program.

name: BPM232 Buddhist Psychology
note: Anderson Todd's Toronto introduction to Buddhist psychology: the Buddha's life, the four noble truths, dependent co-origination and the nature of self.

name: Abnormal Psychology
note: George Atwood's 2012 Rutgers course on abnormal psychology, recorded as two-part lectures covering psychological disorders and their treatment.

name: PSYC 200: Introduction to Psychology
note: Biola's Fall 2013 introductory psychology course: what psychology is, its history and practice, then neuroscience, neurotransmitters and brain organization.

name: Brain Channel
note: UC San Diego's Brain Channel: neuroscientist William Mobley interviews experts on Alzheimer's, cognitive aging and brain health, with some COVID-era interviews.

name: Center for Addiction Research
note: Three short Vanderbilt videos on addiction: sobriety and art during COVID-19, incarceration and addiction, and a conversation with musician Langhorne Slim.

name: Psychiatry Grand Rounds
note: Grand rounds lectures for clinicians from UNM's psychiatry department: diagnosis, medication, bipolar disorder, trauma and community care.

name: Psychology Public Lectures
note: Glenn D. Wilson's Gresham College public lectures on love, sex, happiness, politics, personality disorders and the criminal mind.

name: The Mind and Human Violence
note: Gresham College lectures on the human condition: Gwen Adshead on violence and moral choice, Glenn Wilson on creativity and personality, and more.

name: Why Do We Have Emotions?
note: Robin May's six Gresham College lectures on the biology and psychology of emotion: love, hate, grief, laughter, fear and manipulating emotions.

name: Neuroscience: The Brain and the Mind
note: Three Gresham College lectures on psychosis as a default mental state, the neuroscience of sleep and its disorders, and whether dementia is inevitable.

name: The Right Stuff: Ethics and Moral Psychology
note: Gwen Adshead's three Gresham College lectures linking moral reasoning to medical ethics: consent, privacy, disclosure and what makes a good doctor.

name: Changing Minds and Mental Health
note: Gwen Adshead's three Gresham College psychiatry lectures on how minds change: mental health, mental development and changing risk.

name: Things of Darkness: Human Violence
note: Gwen Adshead's three Gresham College lectures on the nature of human violence, the people who commit it and whether violence can be treated.

name: Mathematics and the Brain
note: Alain Goriely's six Gresham College lectures on the brain through mathematics: illusions, dementia, brain rhythms, networks, cortical folds and brain size.

name: Neurodiversity
note: Three Gresham College lectures on neurodiversity: Maggie Snowling on dyslexia, Francesca Happe on autism and Peter Hill on ADHD.

name: Music and Emotion
note: Jeremy Summerly's Gresham College music-history lectures on nostalgia, love and humour in music; not a psychology course.

name: The Psychology of Finance
note: Alex Edmans's six Gresham College lectures on behavioral finance: investor and CEO mistakes, the psychology of the stock market and nudging better decisions.

name: Living with Mental Health
note: Two Gresham College lectures on mental health: one on living with mental health problems and one on how sleep and mental health affect each other.

name: Mental Health Lectures
note: Six Gresham College lectures on mental wellbeing: the pursuit of happiness, depression, sunshine and sleep, stress at work and doctor-patient communication.

name: Exploring Human Behavior in Finance
note: Raghavendra Rau's six Gresham College lectures on why smart people make poor money decisions: biases, herd behavior, conflicts of interest and financial traps.

name: Psychology, Brain and Mind Lectures
note: Royal Institution lectures on psychology and neuroscience: consciousness with Anil Seth and Mark Solms, memory, addiction, voices, dreams and psychedelics.

name: The Science of Mind, Matter and Curiosity
note: Mixed Royal Institution talks on behaviour change, stress, sleep, sex, voices in the head, psychedelics and mental health, alongside other science topics.

name: Gifford Lectures
note: Michael Gazzaniga's six 2009 Gifford Lectures at Edinburgh on the brain, the split-brain interpreter, free will, the social brain and law.

name: Lunch Hour Lectures: Psychology and Language Sciences
note: UCL lunchtime lectures by psychology and language sciences staff on psychopathy, the social brain, stuttering, deafness and language, giving and attention.

name: Talks by UCL Psychology and Language Sciences Academics
note: Short UCL talks: Sophie Scott on laughter, Susan Michie on what changes behaviour, Nichola Raihani on cooperation, and COVID-era topics.

name: Meet the Psychologists
note: Four one-minute Open University clips in which psychologists explain what psychology is, what you learn studying it and where a degree can lead. [dropped: one-minute promos]

name: Psychology in Sheffield
note: Mixed Sheffield psychology department videos: a virtual tour and graduation alongside short talks on Tetris, nudging, free will and social robots.

name: Society and Behavior
note: Two faculty promo videos from the University of Amsterdam on young people and LGBTQIA+ topics and computational social science; not psychology teaching.

name: RCPsych Lectures
note: Royal College of Psychiatrists lectures for clinicians: a four-part series on adult ADHD with David Nutt and others, plus keynotes and talks on leadership.

name: Mental Health Information
note: Short Royal College of Psychiatrists videos of personal stories: bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, depression, eating disorders, dementia and gambling recovery.

name: Learn at FASS: Psychology
note: Six Simon Fraser videos: why study psychology, forensic psychology, talking about sex, course previews and a talk on Indigenous trauma and survivance.

name: Learn at FASS: Cognitive Science
note: A single two-minute Simon Fraser preview of COGS 100 with Mark Blair, introducing the interdisciplinary study of the mind. [dropped: single course preview]

name: Brain Basics
note: Three one-minute Allen Institute explainers on the brain's building blocks: excitatory neurons, inhibitory neurons and glia.

name: Foundations of Psychology: Concepts and Applications
note: NPTEL introduction to psychology: concepts, intelligence testing, abnormal behaviour and its treatment, and applications to work, education, sport and law.

name: Applied Positive Psychology
note: Dilwar Hussain's NPTEL course on applying positive psychology: interventions, counseling, relationships, kindness, schools and workplace well-being.

name: Psychology of Personality and Individual Differences
note: Dilwar Hussain's NPTEL course on personality: theories and assessment, development, positive traits like empathy and resilience, and links to health and work.

name: Engineering Psychology
note: NPTEL engineering psychology course: human factors topics including multitasking, decision making, motor skill, environmental design and human error.

name: Fundamentals of Language Acquisition
note: Bidisha Som's NPTEL course on how children acquire language: milestones, brain language areas, bilingualism and developmental language disorders.

name: Basics of Experimental Design for Cognitive Psychology
note: NPTEL course on research methods for cognitive psychology: the scientific method, theories, and descriptive, correlational and experimental designs.

name: Bayesian Data Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences
note: NPTEL course on Bayesian data analysis for behavioral scientists, built up from sets, probability axioms and distributions toward Bayesian inference.

name: Mental Health and Wellbeing
note: NPTEL course on adolescent mental health and wellbeing: stress and anxiety, relationships, social media, self-care, body image and mindfulness.

name: Social Behavior and the Brain: An Introduction to Social Neuroscience
note: NPTEL introduction to social neuroscience: how the brain processes the self, other people and faces, across 40 lectures.

name: Mathematical Tools for Cognitive Science
note: NPTEL math primer for cognitive science students: numbers, equations, graphs, functions, logarithms and exponentials, built up from the basics. [dropped: calculus and linear algebra, not psychology]

name: Positive Psychology
note: NPTEL positive psychology course: an introduction to psychology and research methods, then character strengths and virtues, happiness and well-being.

name: Classics in Neuroscience
note: Varadhan SKM's NPTEL course at IIT Madras on the origins of modern neuroscience: the 1950s, DNA and molecular biology, growth factors and classic discoveries.

name: Principles and Practice of Sleep Medicine
note: NPTEL sleep medicine course: sleep architecture and neurophysiology, deprivation, insomnia, narcolepsy, parasomnias and sleep apnea.

name: Organizational Behaviour
note: NPTEL organizational behaviour course in 56 lectures, covering perception, personality and other psychology of people at work.

name: Yoga and Positive Psychology for Managing Career and Life
note: NPTEL course (Jan 2023) combining positive psychology and yoga for self-management, wellbeing and career, in 94 short lecture videos.

name: Introductory Neuroscience and Neuro-Instrumentation
note: NPTEL course pairing neuroscience basics (CNS structure, membrane potential, neocortical circuits) with instrumentation: biopotentials, EEG and MEMS.

name: Psychology
note: Indian UGC lectures on psychology: clinical psychology, emotional intelligence, motivation, happiness, educational psychology and organisational behaviour.

name: PSY409 Positive Psychology
note: Complete 45-lecture positive psychology course from the Virtual University of Pakistan; videos are titled by lecture number only.

name: PSY512 Gender Issues in Psychology
note: Complete 45-lecture course on gender issues in psychology from the Virtual University of Pakistan; videos are titled by lecture number only.

name: PSY514 Consumer Psychology
note: Complete 45-lecture consumer psychology course from the Virtual University of Pakistan; videos are titled by lecture number only.

name: PSY631 Psychological Testing and Measurement
note: Complete 45-lecture course on psychological testing and measurement from the Virtual University of Pakistan; videos are titled by lecture number only.

name: EDU303 Child Development
note: Complete 45-lecture child development course from the Virtual University of Pakistan; videos are titled by lecture number only.

name: MGT502 Organizational Behaviour
note: Complete 45-lecture organizational behaviour course from the Virtual University of Pakistan; videos are titled by lecture number only.

name: GENED 1066: Rationality
note: Steven Pinker's Harvard Gen Ed course on rationality: logic, probability, Bayes, decision and game theory, cognitive biases, with guest lectures by Gawande, Sunstein, Lewis, Chenoweth and MacAskill.

name: PSY 1: Introduction to Psychological Science
note: Steven Pinker's Harvard intro psychology lectures (Spring 2021): evolution, the brain, perception, memory, language, development; 8 of the 23 lectures were archived by Harvard and can't play.
